results.title: Maltese sim racer heading to Global Esports Games in December
results.description: Maltese e-sports driver Aaron Debattista secured himself a spot in this year's Global Esports Games earlier this month. Debattista will be representing Malta in Los Angeles, California, USA in the first week of December. Following two qualification races in the first weekend of September, Debattista has managed to send Malta to the Global Esports Games after securing a qualification slot in its iRacing series. iRacing is an online racing simulation game where players can drive around the virtual creations of real-life tracks and real-life cars, from the comfort of their set-ups. Competitive sim racers have a serious set-up for these virtual races, including wide monitors accompanied by their own remote steering wheel, pedals, a racing seat, and the lot. Debattista is honoured to be representing Malta and said he is "immensely proud" to be competing on Malta's behalf in three months' time. The Global Esports Games will be taking place on 1-7 December 2026. He believes that he is the first Maltese to qualify for this particular e-sim racing competition. He mentioned that he will be competing against high-calibre, professional e-sports racers from 54 other countries. During this qualification stage, countries from Europe, Africa, the Middle East, Asia, and the Americas took part. With 10 qualification slots available among the pool of 28 European, African, and some Middle Eastern countries, Debattista qualified in 10 th place. Racing around virtual tracks of the Virginia International Raceway and the WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca, he started the first race in 13 th place and finished in 11 th , just a hair away from the driver ahead of him. Debattista then began the second race in 9 th place and finished in 8 th place to finish 10 th in the overall standings and nip qualification for Malta to compete on the world stage. He contently told The Malta Independent that he "wasn't very far away" from some of the drivers ahead of him, some of whom make a living as professional sim racers. All drivers in this competition were using the same car within the online racing simulation game: a Ferrari 296 Challenge. All cars used the same fixed/common set-up, to guarantee equal competition among the sim racers. Debattista earned the opportunity to be Malta's representative during this e-sports series after winning a championship series hosted by the Malta Esports Association. Debattista said that he competes semi-professionally, since he does not compete in simulation racing full-time. Debattista is a local sim racer who competes with the e-sports team Intercomp VMD Simsport. Speaking to this newsroom, he thanked everyone in his team for pushing him towards this result and supporting him throughout, as well as his friends and family. He said that all the support he has received "up to this very moment" helped him qualify. Till he competes in the USA in December, Debattista will keep striving as a driver in hopes that he keeps improving and performs for Malta in on this stage. "The best is yet to come," he said.
